When non-Hermitian perturbation is small, the original knot topology is preserved (Figure 1).


Code
from IPython.display import HTML

def display_html(nonHermticity):
    ES_file = f"assets/ES_nH={nonHermticity}.html"
    SG_file = f"assets/SG_nH={nonHermticity}.html"
    # Display the saved HTML files side by side.
    return HTML(f"""
    <div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between;">
        <iframe src="{ES_file}" width="800" height="500" style="border: none;"></iframe>
        <iframe src="{SG_file}" width="800" height="500" style="border: none;"></iframe>
    </div>
    """)

display_html(0.1)





    
        
        
    
    


Figure 1: Non-Hermiticity = 0.1. The original knot topology is preserved.




When non-Hermiticity is prevalent enough, the exceptional surface starts to touch itself, leading to a topology transition — the skeleton (i.e., medial axis) of the exceptional surface becomes a knotted graph (a.k.a. spatial multigraph).
As the non-Hermiticity evolves, the knotted graph topology evolves accordingly, leading to a plethora of exotic 3D spatial geometries (Figure 2, Figure 3).


Code
display_html(0.2)





    
        
        
    
    


Figure 2: Non-Hermiticity = 0.2. The exceptional surface starts to touch itself, and the skeleton of the exceptional surface becomes a knotted graph.






Code
display_html(0.5)





    
        
        
    
    


Figure 3: Non-Hermiticity = 0.5. As non-Hermiticity evolves, the knotted graph topology evolves accordingly, leading to a plethora of exotic 3D spatial geometries.

df = px.data.iris()
fig = px.scatter(df, x="sepal_width", y="sepal_length",

                 marginal_y="violin",

                #  trendline="ols",

fig.show()

title: Quarto Website Demo for Scientific Communication
text:
Quarto is an open-source scientific and technical publishing system that builds on standard tools like Pandoc and Jupyter to create a powerful and flexible authoring environment.
Here are some of the highlights:

title: Quarto Website Demo for Scientific Communication
text:
Author with Ease and Flexibility
One can simply author content in familiar Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) or use a single, plain-text source file (.qmd) with any text editor you prefer, and in one click render publishable documents in multiple formats, and release them as interactive websites.

title: Quarto Website Demo for Scientific Communication
Quarto Website Demo for Scientific Communication
section: Full LaTeX Support and Multiple Output Formats
text:
Full LaTeX Support and Multiple Output Formats
Quarto provides a first-class authoring experience for \(\LaTeX\), preserving the features that academic publishing relies on.

Write complex equations, like a non-Hermitian Hamiltonian, using standard \(\LaTeX\) syntax: \[
H = H_0 + i\gamma \sigma_y
\tag{1}\]
Effortlessly add citations, and cross-reference equations, figures, tables, and theorems. For example Figure 1 and Equation 1 can be easily referenced by @fig-kg and @eq-H.
Generate multiple high-quality output formats from a single source file, including publication-ready PDFs, responsive HTML websites, MS Word documents, and ePub books.

title: Quarto Website Demo for Scientific Communication
text:
Interactive Presentations with Reveal.js
Transform your research into compelling, interactive presentations for conferences or lectures using Reveal.js. You can reuse content, code, and visualizations directly from your manuscript in your slides, ensuring consistency and saving valuable time.

title: Quarto Website Demo for Scientific Communication
text:
Effortless Publishing and Sharing
Share your work with the world with a single command. Quarto simplifies the process of publishing your entire project as a polished website to free hosting platforms. - GitHub Pages: quarto publish gh-pages - Netlify: quarto publish netlify - Posit Connect and other services are also supported.

title: Quarto Website Demo for Scientific Communication
section: Interactive Courses, Books, and Supplemental Materials
text:
Interactive Courses, Books, and Supplemental Materials
Beyond single papers, Quarto is a complete scientific and technical publishing system. It is ideal for creating comprehensive resources for the scientific community. - Paper Supplements: Build an interactive website to accompany your paper, featuring executable code, interactive data visualizations, and extended appendices. - Online Books: Author entire books with chapters, parts, and bibliographies. - Courses & Lecture Notes: Develop full course websites with lecture notes that mix theory, equations, videos, and live, executable code examples that students can run and modify in their browser.
